record.paper_title: Where First-Order and Monadic Second-Order Logic Coincide
record.context_brief: Composition theorems for MSO variants with parity
record.original_question: For variants of monadic second-order logic such as MSO with parity predicates, which test whether quantified relations have even cardinality, what kind of first-order logic is needed to combine the logical types of an unbounded number of substructures, and for which such monadic second-order logics can those type-combination methods be developed?

evidence.quote: Another direction is to consider other kinds of monadic second-order logics like MSO with parity predicates, which test whether bound relations have even cardinality.
Which kind of first-order logics do we need to combine the types of which kinds of monadic second-order logics?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\tau$ be a finite relational vocabulary. Monadic second-order logic ($\mathrm{MSO}$) over $\tau$ extends first-order logic by allowing quantification over sets (unary relations) of elements. A composition method (in the style of Feferman–Vaught and Shelah) computes, for a structure built from substructures $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ via some gluing operation, the $\mathrm{MSO}$-type (up to a given quantifier rank) of the whole structure as a function — expressible in some logic $\mathcal{L}$ over an index structure — of the $\mathrm{MSO}$-types of the parts. When the number of parts is bounded, $\mathcal{L}$ can be chosen to be propositional, but when the number of substructures is unbounded, one needs a logic $\mathcal{L}$ capable of aggregating an unbounded family of types.

Consider variants of $\mathrm{MSO}$ obtained by adding parity predicates: for each set variable $X$, an atomic formula $\mathrm{Even}(X)$ holding iff $|X|$ is finite and even (and, more generally, modular counting predicates $|X| \equiv k \pmod{m}$, giving counting $\mathrm{MSO}$, denoted $\mathrm{CMSO}$).

Problem. Identify, for $\mathrm{MSO}$ extended with parity (or modular counting) predicates, a first-order-style logic $\mathcal{L}$ — to be characterized precisely — that suffices to combine the logical types of an unbounded number of substructures into the type of the whole structure, and determine the class of such extensions of $\mathrm{MSO}$ for which a composition method of this form can be developed. Concretely: produce a composition theorem in which, for every quantifier-rank bound $n$, there is a function expressible in $\mathcal{L}$ that maps the multiset (or indexed family) of rank-$n$ types of the substructures to the rank-$n$ type of the composed structure, and delimit the variants of monadic second-order logic with parity/counting predicates to which this approach applies.
artifact.category_tag: Composition theorems for monadic second-order logic
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search returned general references on MSO, counting MSO (CMSO with modular counting predicates), and composition-style results, but no source that resolves the specific question of identifying the appropriate first-order logic for combining types of unboundedly many substructures for MSO with parity predicates. The status of the question is therefore unclear from the available evidence.

status_evidence.snippet: Background on MSO and its variants including counting extensions.
status_evidence.claim: Counting/parity extensions of MSO are well-known, but no resolution of the composition question is indicated.

status_evidence.title: On the Monadic Second-Order Transduction Hierarchy
status_evidence.claim: Does not directly address composition for MSO+parity with unbounded substructures.
